sections.heading: AC Repair
body: The house is crawling past 80, the vents blow lukewarm air, or the unit outside runs and runs without cooling anything.

Air conditioners fail in a few predictable places: a weak capacitor, a dirty coil, a tired motor, or a refrigerant leak. We find the real cause, explain it plainly and fix it. If an old unit isn't worth repairing, we say so.

sections.heading: Furnace Repair
body: A furnace that quits rarely says why. It clicks and never lights, runs two minutes and shuts down, or blows cold air while the house gets colder.

The cause is often small: an igniter, a flame sensor, a clogged filter or a failing blower motor. We show you what failed and fix it. A cracked heat exchanger is a safety matter, and we'll tell you plainly if that's what we find.

sections.heading: When a Repair Stops Making Sense
body: If you've paid for two or three repairs in a couple of years and the equipment is old, a new system is usually the cheaper road. Sometimes the honest answer is one more repair instead.

We install new heating and cooling equipment too, and we'll give you our real opinion before you spend that kind of money. A system that is sized and set up badly runs hard and wears out early, so the installation matters as much as the equipment.

sections.heading: Heat Pumps, Motors and Maintenance
body: We also repair heat pumps and replace blower and condenser motors that have started making noise. Commercial heating and cooling is part of the work too.

A dirty filter, a coil caked with dust and a motor running dry wear a system out a little more each season. A check before the heavy season catches them while they're cheap. We offer maintenance plans, so ask about one when you call.

sections.heading: What You Can Count On
body: **A price you can follow.** We break down the cost of the work, with no surprise charges.
**Answers in plain words.** We explain what failed and why, so you decide with the facts in front of you.
**A clean house when we leave.** A repair shouldn't leave you a second job.
**Work we stand behind.** We do the job right the first time, and we stand by it.

sections.heading: When to Call
body: The house won't cool below 80 no matter how long the unit runs. The air from the vents is lukewarm. The outdoor unit hums but the fan isn't spinning, or the breaker trips every time it starts.

Ice on the copper line outside, water around the indoor unit and a system that cycles on and off every few minutes are all signs to turn it off and call. Running a struggling air conditioner makes a small repair bigger.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong
body: Most AC failures come from a short list of parts, and knowing the list helps you follow what a technician tells you.
**Capacitor.** This small part gives the compressor and fan motor the jolt they need to start. When it weakens, the unit hums and won't run. It's one of the most common and cheapest repairs.
**Dirty coil or clogged filter.** Dust on the coil and a choked filter cut the airflow until the coil freezes into a block of ice. The fix is cleaning and finding out why it got that way.
**Low refrigerant.** An air conditioner doesn't use up refrigerant. If it's low, there's a leak, and adding more without fixing the leak is money that drains away again.
**Fan or compressor motor.** Motors wear, and a noisy or slow-spinning motor is a warning. Replacing it early is a far smaller job than waiting for it to fail.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?

Replacement starts to make sense when the unit is old, repairs are piling up, or the problem is something like a failed compressor on a system that's already near the end of its life. A big repair bill on an old unit is often money you'd rather put toward a new one.
We tell you which situation you're in, and we'll tell you if the answer is to repair. We also install new air conditioning equipment when it's time.

sections.heading: Signs Your Furnace Needs a Technician
body: The thermostat is calling for heat and nothing happens. You hear clicking but the burners never light. The furnace starts, runs a couple of minutes and shuts off, over and over.
Other signs are quieter. Some rooms stay cold, the blower screams or rattles, or the air coming out isn't warm. Any of these is worth a call before the coldest week of the year.

sections.heading: What Usually Stops the Heat
body: A furnace has several steps to go through before it heats your house, and a failure at any one stops the whole thing. That's why most no-heat calls turn out to be a small part and not a new furnace.
**Igniter.** The part that lights the burner wears out with use. A cracked or weak igniter means the furnace tries to start and can't.

**Flame sensor.** This small rod tells the furnace that the burner lit. When it gets coated with residue, the furnace shuts down after a few seconds as a safety measure. Cleaning or replacing it is a simple repair.
**Filter and airflow.** A clogged filter makes the furnace overheat and shut itself off. It's the cheapest fix there is, and the reason some furnaces cycle on and off.
**Blower motor.** The blower moves the warm air through the house. When it fails, the furnace can run and heat and you still get little or no warmth in the rooms.

sections.heading: The Problem That Isn't Small
body: A cracked heat exchanger is different. It's the metal chamber that keeps burner exhaust apart from the air you breathe, and a crack in it is a safety problem, not an inconvenience.

If a technician finds one, you'll hear it from us straight, with what it means and what your options are. Whatever your furnace is doing, a working carbon monoxide detector on every floor is worth having.

sections.heading: How We Handle a Furnace Call
body: We diagnose first. A technician finds the actual cause and shows you what failed.

Then you get a full breakdown of what the repair costs, with no surprise charges at the end. When the work is done, we clean up after ourselves, because a furnace closet full of dust and old parts is not your job.

sections.quote: Sam and his team installed a new furnace for me. They were timely, worked efficiently and cleaned up the mess afterwards. I highly recommend Integrity Heating and Cooling and will use them again.

sections.heading: Repair or New Furnace?
body: Repair is the right answer most of the time. An igniter, a sensor or a motor costs far less than a furnace, and the furnace goes on heating your house.
A new furnace starts to make sense when the furnace is old, the repairs keep coming, or the heat exchanger has failed. Spending a lot on an old furnace is often money better put toward a new one.
We tell you which side of that line you're on. If it's time to replace, we install new furnaces and heating systems too, and we stand by that work.

sections.quote: Integrity Heating and Cooling replaced my whole HVAC system and left me with full confidence that everything was installed to last with no problems. They were very thorough and efficient and got the job done. I wasn’t sure I could get a fair quote along with great work ethic but these guys proved me wrong!

sections.heading: Keeping a Furnace Healthy
body: Furnaces fail hardest in the first cold snap, after sitting idle all summer. Dust builds up, parts stiffen and a weak igniter finally gives out.
A check before heating season catches those things while it's still warm outside. We offer maintenance plans, so ask about one when you call. Changing the filter on a schedule helps too.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: If you can do it safely, check a few things first. Make sure the thermostat is set to heat and the batteries are fresh. Check that the furnace switch is on, and that the filter isn't packed with dust.
If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas company before anything else. Otherwise, if the furnace still won't run, call us.
